findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/cross-host-review.ts:922-933 — the six-line "Bug10" explanatory comment block about the trusted policy ceiling is duplicated verbatim twice in immediate succession (lines 922-927 and 928-933). No functional impact (tsc clean, validate green), but it is a merge/rebase copy-paste artifact in newly added code that misleads readers into thinking two distinct invariants are being documented.

packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:1730-1732 — readManagedReviewProposalInvocationFromFd calls readFileSync(fd,'utf8') to consume the ENTIRE descriptor and only afterwards checks Buffer.byteLength(raw)>64*1024. The size guard therefore cannot bound memory: a descriptor delivering, e.g., 500 MiB is fully buffered before the 64 KiB error is raised. Reachable only through the framework-provisioned LATTICE_MANAGED_REVIEW_INVOCATION_FD (set at core/host-run.ts:1364) under the documented same-uid local trust ceiling, so this is defense-in-depth rather than an exploitable path; the check as written does not deliver the bound it states.

packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:652-657 — atomicWrite writes a temp file then renameSync/chmodSync without a finally-block cleanup, so any throw from rename or chmod (permissions, ENOSPC after the write, interrupted syscall) leaks an orphan `<path>.tmp-<pid>-<hex>` inside the durable managed run directory. The sibling helper writeExclusive at line 659 handles exactly this with `finally { unlinkIfPresent(temp) }`, so the omission is an inconsistency in the same file. Orphans accumulate in run directories that later feed digest/seal scans and retention GC.
